narrative.northStar: The House on Cream and Navy
narrative.overview:
DineChain is dressed as a modern Vietnamese restaurant house: a warm cream ground, deep navy for everything that frames the room (the staff rail, the guest band, the kitchen display, occupied tables, full-colour blocks), and one royal blue that says "act here". The brand is carried by two things only: large, narrow condensed serif type and food photography. Everything else (labels, sentences, form text, staff buttons) is a quiet grotesk. The visual style was taken from a user-pinned restaurant website (pizza4ps.com/vn) as a reference for palette, type, composition and buttons only; none of its identity is used.

The system runs in two modes. The guest home persuades: a full-bleed food photo, a stacked giant serif list of the ways to eat, a royal-blue panel counting open branches in boxed digits, a navy/sand split, and a photo-led menu grid. The guest ordering pages and the whole staff app under /nha-hang operate: dense, flat, cream work surfaces with hairline rules, serif for the numbers the eye must find first (table numbers, prices, totals, change, quantities, codes) and large touch targets. The kitchen display is the navy room: deep navy ground, cream type, nothing on paper.

The world replaces an earlier chalkboard skin (board green, chalk colours, handwritten face) and refuses the grey SaaS POS. Surfaces are flat; depth comes from tone and hairlines, not shadow.
keyCharacteristics: Cream ground, sand panels, paper cards; deep navy frames the room and fills the blocks.
One royal-blue accent for links, focus, selection, the guest's forward action and live counters.
Condensed serif (Noto Serif Display, width 68%) for headings and figures; Be Vietnam Pro for every word of UI.
Pill controls for staff, hairline ovals with serif capitals for guest calls to action.
The boxed-digit counter for live numbers; a clean drawn rule strikes through what is gone.
Status is always a word plus an icon, never colour alone.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Royal blue means "act here" or "you are here": links, focus, selection, live counters and the single forward action of a guest page. It is never decoration, never a heading colour, never a background for content.

rules.name: The Navy Frames the Room Rule
rules.body: Navy holds navigation, the guest band, the kitchen display and full-colour blocks. Work happens on cream, sand and paper; the kitchen's own controls are the only working surface on navy.

rules.name: The Wash and Ink Rule
rules.body: On light surfaces a status hue appears as its wash behind its ink, with a word and an icon. Raw status hues are for meters, strikes and marks on navy only.

rules.name: The Serif Speaks Rule
rules.body: The condensed serif writes headings, prices, table numbers, totals, change, quantities, codes, counts and clocks. Sentences, labels, form text, dish names in lists and staff buttons are always Be Vietnam Pro. The guest oval is the one control set in serif capitals.

rules.name: The Label Names a Group Rule
rules.body: Uppercase small labels name a group of data (a category, an area, a column, a field). They never float above a headline as a decorative eyebrow.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Grotesk amounts use tabular numerals and sit right-aligned; VND, no decimals; every total shows its proof (subtotal, discount, points, VAT).

rules.name: The Hairline, Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Separate with a 1px rule or a change of ground. Shadow is reserved for floating layers; selection is a blue ring, never a shadow.

dos: **Do** give each staff screen one solid navy pill as its primary action; other actions are outlines.
**Do** write figures in the condensed serif at width 68%: table numbers, prices, totals, change, quantities, codes, clocks.
**Do** use the boxed-digit counter for live numbers and give it an accessible label.
**Do** strike sold-out or cancelled items with the drawn rule and keep them visible.
**Do** pair every status with a word and an icon, on its wash with its ink.
**Do** separate with 1px hairlines and changes of ground; keep panels flat.
**Do** lead the guest home with food photography and let serif type sit directly on it under a navy shade.
**Do** keep touch targets at 42px or more, 52 to 56px on POS and kitchen actions.
donts: **Don't** introduce a second accent hue; royal blue is the only one.
**Don't** set sentences, labels, form text or staff buttons in the serif.
**Don't** place uppercase labels above headlines as decorative eyebrows.
**Don't** use shadows on resting cards or for selection.
**Don't** use oval buttons in the staff app; they belong to guest pages.
**Don't** round photos or counter digit boxes.
**Don't** bring back the chalkboard skin (board green, chalk colours, a handwritten face) or drift toward a grey SaaS POS.
**Don't** use the reference site's logo, name, photos or copy; no DineChain logo or tagline exists, so the wordmark stays text.
